study.title: PHA / HAZOP – Propane storage and propane–air dilution system (worked example)
study.unit: Utilities – LPG (propane) storage, vaporisation and propane–air (SNG) dilution
study.project: PHA revalidation – propane storage and dilution system
study.scope: Propane from the road-tanker connection at the unloading bay (node 301: unloading arm, vapour compressors C-01/C-02/C-03, liquid line via ROV-1 and inlet valves ROV-11/21/31 to the three storage bullets T-1/T-2/T-3), the liquid draw-off, pumps P-01/P-02, vaporisers VAP-01/VAP-02 and regulator PCV-01 to the 1.5 barg vapour header and the steel-works consumers (node 302), and the propane–air mixing station MX-01 with air blowers B-01/B-02, ratio control and surge tank ST-01 supplying propane–air to the reheat-furnace and ladle-preheater burners (node 303).
study.exclusions: Road tanker itself (owned by the supplier); burner internals and burner management at the users; fire-water pump house; electrical substation. Propane deliveries on public roads.
study.basis: Receive propane from 20 t road tankers (tanker design 20.6 barg) without overfilling or overpressuring the bullets (design 17.5 barg, design minimum temperature −45 °C, maximum fill 85 % of volume); vaporise propane and deliver vapour at 1.5 barg; blend it with air to a propane–air mixture of about 55 % propane (well above the upper flammable limit of 9.5 %) at 0.8 barg. Source pressures in kg/cm² are converted to barg. All values are illustrative.
study.modes: Tanker unloading (about 150 deliveries a year), normal supply, vaporiser change-over, start-up of the mixing station after a shutdown, maintenance isolation and gas-free, power failure and restart

sessions.notes: Node 301 (tanker to storage) – source worksheet reviewed, completed and corrected; overfill referred to FT-PR-01, releases to BT-PR-01 / ETA-PR-01.
Node 302 (supply to consumers) – pumps, vaporisers, regulator.
Node 303 (propane dilution) – flammable-mixture scenario referred to FT-PR-02 and BT-PR-02. Study closed; FMECA on 12 Nov.

nodes.name: Node 301 – Road tanker unloading to propane storage T-1/T-2/T-3
nodes.batteryLimits: From the road-tanker liquid and vapour couplings (unloading arm with emergency release coupling ERC-1) via liquid line ROV-1 and the tank inlet valves ROV-11/21/31 to bullets T-1/T-2/T-3; vapour return by compressors C-01/C-02/C-03 from the bullets to the tanker
nodes.description: Transfer liquid propane from a 20 t road tanker into one storage bullet at a time by vapour compression, without overfilling, overpressure or release
nodes.designParams: Bullets T-1/T-2/T-3: 3 x 60 m3, design 17.5 barg, design min. temperature −45 °C, PSV-11/21/31 at 17.5 barg; tanker design 20.6 barg (source: 21 kg/cm2); compressor trip at 20.6 barg; maximum fill 85 % (LT-11/21/31 LAH 80 %, LAHH 85 % → closes ROV-11/21/31)
nodes.operatingParams: Unloading 60–90 min per delivery, about 150 deliveries a year; storage 5–12 barg depending on ambient temperature
nodes.materials: Propane (extremely flammable liquefied gas; boiling point −42 °C; vapour denser than air; flammable 2.1–9.5 %)

nodes.name: Node 302 – Supply of propane to consumers (pumps, vaporisers, PCV-01)
nodes.batteryLimits: From the bullet outlet valves ROV-12/22/32 via pumps P-01/P-02 to water-bath vaporisers VAP-01/VAP-02, pressure regulator PCV-01 (with slam-shut SSV-01) to the 1.5 barg vapour header and the steel-works consumers
nodes.description: Draw liquid propane from storage, vaporise it completely and deliver dry vapour at 1.5 barg to the users and the mixing station
nodes.designParams: Liquid lines 25 barg design; vaporisers 25 barg (liquid side), PSV-02 at 20 barg; vapour header 3.5 barg design; PSV-03 at 3.0 barg; TSL-01 low vapour outlet temperature trip at 10 °C; LSH-01 high liquid level in vaporiser trip
nodes.operatingParams: Liquid 8–12 barg; vapour 1.4–1.6 barg, 20–40 °C; up to 1 200 kg/h propane
nodes.materials: Propane liquid and vapour; hot water in the vaporiser baths

nodes.name: Node 303 – Propane dilution system (propane–air mixing station)
nodes.batteryLimits: From the propane vapour header (XV-01) and the air blowers B-01/B-02 (XV-02) through the venturi mixer MX-01 with ratio controller FFIC-01 and calorimeter AT-01 to surge tank ST-01 and the propane–air header to the reheat-furnace and ladle-preheater burners
nodes.description: Blend propane vapour with air to a propane–air mixture of 55 % propane (Wobbe index matched to natural gas, above the upper flammable limit) at 0.8 barg, and never let the mixture approach the flammable range
nodes.designParams: Mixer and surge tank ST-01 3.5 barg design, PSV-04 at 2.0 barg; explosion vent panel EP-01 on ST-01; flame arrester FA-01 on the propane–air header; PSLL-01 low propane pressure trip stops B-01/B-02 and closes XV-01/XV-02
nodes.materials: Propane vapour; air; propane–air mixture (flammable if propane falls below about 10 % in air)

deviations.deviation: No / less flow – compressor malfunction
deviations.consequence: Low or no filling rate into the storage tank (source); longer tanker stay at the bay increases the exposure time for drive-away and traffic impact
deviations.comments: Source deviation 'No / less flow – compressor malfunction'.

deviations.deviation: No flow – ROV-1 stuck closed while the compressor runs
deviations.consequence: No filling of the storage tank; pressure rises in the tanker as the compressor keeps pushing vapour (source) – tanker relief valve may lift at the bay
deviations.comments: Source safeguards: compressor trip at 21 kg/cm2 (20.6 barg), tanker designed for 21 kg/cm2, pressure gauge and tanker PSV. Source remark: include PSV testing in the maintenance schedule (R-003).

deviations.deviation: More flow – high pressure difference between tanker and tank
deviations.consequence: Static charge generated in the line during liquid filling (source); spark discharge at an unbonded flange can ignite a small leak
deviations.comments: Source recommendation no. 1 (earthing jumpers at every flange) is R-001.

deviations.deviation: Higher pressure in the bullet during unloading
deviations.consequence: Bullet pressure towards the 17.5 barg relief setting; PSV-11/21/31 lift and vent propane vapour; flammable cloud at the tank farm
deviations.lopaNotes: L-09: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 (Safety, RRF 3); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only; L-10: Meets target (Safety); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only; L-11: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 (Safety, RRF 5.82); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only

deviations.deviation: Lower pressure
deviations.consequence: No hazard to the bullets – propane vapour pressure stays above atmospheric down to −42 °C; slower unloading only

deviations.deviation: Higher level in storage tank T-1/T-2/T-3 (overfill)
deviations.consequence: Source: tank pressurisation. Correctly: the bullet fills liquid-full; liquid propane reaches the relief valves – liquid relief and a large two-phase release at the tank farm; hydraulic overpressure of the liquid-full bullet as it warms
deviations.comments: The source credited only the LT closing the ROV, whose transmitter is also the gauge the operator uses – not independent. Quantified in fault tree FT-PR-01 (top 1.9E-3 /yr); overfill is threat T1 of bow tie BT-PR-01. Likelihood after safeguards from the calculated frequency 1.9E-3 /yr.
deviations.lopaNotes: L-01: SIL 2 needed (Safety, RRF 505); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-02: SIL 3 needed (Safety, RRF 1.5E+3); with proposed IPLs: SIL 1 needed – accepted IPLs only; L-03: Above SIL 3 – change the design (Safety, RRF 1.5E+4); with proposed IPLs: SIL 2 needed – accepted IPLs only

deviations.deviation: Higher temperature – external fire
deviations.consequence: Fire and explosion hazard; high pressure (source); flame impingement on the vapour space of a bullet or tanker weakens the shell – BLEVE with fireball and fragments
deviations.comments: Source safeguards: PRV-01, gauges, gas detectors GLD-1/2/3, water sprinklers for the tanks and the unloading station, PSV. BLEVE is an end state of event tree ETA-PR-01.

deviations.deviation: Lower temperature – auto-refrigeration
deviations.consequence: Source: 'no issue'. Correctly: carbon steel below its minimum design temperature becomes brittle; a pressurised bullet or line can fail by brittle fracture – sudden large release; cold burns to operators
deviations.comments: Corrected source entry. Brittle fracture is threat T5 of bow tie BT-PR-01.

deviations.deviation: Release during transfer – hose / arm failure
deviations.consequence: Liquid propane release at the unloading bay at up to 10 barg; large flammable cloud (heavier than air); jet fire if ignited; exposure of the tanker
deviations.comments: Not in the source worksheet. Threat T2 of bow tie BT-PR-01; isolation by fault tree FT-PR-03.

deviations.deviation: Tanker drive-away while still connected
deviations.consequence: Arm or hose pulled apart – liquid release from both the tanker and the plant side; severe if the excess-flow valves do not close
deviations.comments: Not in the source worksheet. Threat T3 of bow tie BT-PR-01.
deviations.lopaNotes: L-07: SIL 1 needed (Safety, RRF 30); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-08: SIL 1 needed (Safety, RRF 15); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only

deviations.deviation: Impurity / concentration
deviations.consequence: Source: not applicable. Water can freeze in regulators and drains; butane raises the dew point – liquid in the vapour header (see N02)
deviations.comments: Source entries 'Concentration – NA' and 'Impurity – NA' reviewed: a delivery-quality check was added to the checklist.

deviations.deviation: Utility failure – power
deviations.consequence: No transfer of propane from tanker to storage tank; compressors C-01/C-02/C-03 stop (source). All ROVs and SVs close (source) – safe state, but the gas detection and ESD are lost if the UPS fails
deviations.comments: Source recommendation no. 2 (diesel generator for back-up power) is R-002.

deviations.deviation: Maintenance – opening equipment that still contains propane
deviations.consequence: Propane release at the point of work; flash fire; cold burns

deviations.deviation: No liquid flow to the vaporisers
deviations.consequence: Loss of propane vapour to the users and the mixing station; burners trip on low pressure; at the mixer, air may continue – see N03-01

deviations.deviation: Pump cavitation / loss of suction
deviations.consequence: Pump dry running – seal failure and liquid propane leak at the pump

deviations.deviation: Higher pressure in the vapour header
deviations.consequence: Vapour header (3.5 barg design) and users' fuel trains over-pressured – flange leaks, burner over-firing

deviations.deviation: Low vapour temperature – liquid carry-over from the vaporiser
deviations.consequence: Liquid propane carried into the vapour header; liquid at regulators and burners – flare-ups, over-firing, cold embrittlement of carbon-steel piping

deviations.deviation: High liquid level in the vaporiser shell
deviations.consequence: Liquid carry-over to the header (as N02-04)

deviations.deviation: Vaporiser overpressure – liquid side
deviations.consequence: Rupture of the vaporiser tube bundle – propane into the water bath and its vent

deviations.deviation: Propane in the vaporiser hot-water circuit
deviations.consequence: Propane carried to the hot-water tank vent – flammable atmosphere at the boiler house

deviations.deviation: Leak from the liquid lines / pump seals
deviations.consequence: Liquid propane release at the pump area; flash fire or jet fire; escalation to the bullets

deviations.deviation: Heavier hydrocarbons in the vapour (butane-rich propane)
deviations.consequence: Re-condensation in the cold vapour header in winter; change in heating value at the users

deviations.deviation: Loss of power to the vaporisers and pumps
deviations.consequence: Loss of supply to the users (controlled trip); on restart, liquid carry-over if the bath is cold

deviations.deviation: Less / no propane to the mixer while air continues – mixture moves into the flammable range
deviations.consequence: Propane fraction falls from 55 % towards the flammable range (below 9.5 % in air) – explosive mixture in the mixer, surge tank ST-01 and the header to the burners; ignition at a burner flashes back – internal explosion of ST-01 and the header
deviations.comments: Key scenario of the dilution system. Quantified in fault tree FT-PR-02 (top 1.2E-2 /yr); threat T1 of bow tie BT-PR-02. Likelihood after safeguards from the calculated frequency 1.2E-2 /yr.
deviations.lopaNotes: L-04: SIL 2 needed (Safety, RRF 875); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-05: SIL 2 needed (Safety, RRF 175); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-06: SIL 3 needed (Safety, RRF 1.1E+3); with proposed IPLs: SIL 1 needed – accepted IPLs only

deviations.deviation: More air than set (ratio controller failure)
deviations.consequence: Lower heating value at the burners (flame instability); if severe, mixture approaches the flammable range (as N03-01)

deviations.deviation: Propane back-flow into the air blowers
deviations.consequence: Propane in the blower suction – flammable mixture at the blower motor (not Ex-rated); blower fire

deviations.deviation: Higher pressure in the mixer / surge tank
deviations.consequence: Surge tank ST-01 (3.5 barg design) over-pressured – flange leak of propane–air

deviations.deviation: Mixture outside specification at the burners
deviations.consequence: Flame instability or over-firing at the reheat-furnace and ladle-preheater burners; flame-out with fuel flow (users' BMS)

deviations.deviation: Start-up with air in the mixer, surge tank or header
deviations.consequence: Flammable propane–air mixture in ST-01 and the header during start-up; ignition at the first burner light-off – internal explosion
deviations.comments: Threat T2 of bow tie BT-PR-02.

deviations.deviation: Flashback from the burners into the propane–air header
deviations.consequence: Flame propagation into the header and surge tank – deflagration
deviations.comments: Threat T3 of bow tie BT-PR-02.

deviations.deviation: Leak of propane–air from the mixer or header
deviations.consequence: Flammable release near the furnace building (many ignition sources); flash fire

deviations.deviation: Power failure at the mixing station
deviations.consequence: Blowers stop; propane continues at full pressure to the users (heating value too high) unless XV-01 closes; on restart, sequence must re-establish propane before air

causes.text: Tank inlet ROV-11/21/31 closed (wrong tank selected or trip)
More pressure difference in tanker and tank (source)
Compressor run at full speed on a near-empty tank
Tank inlet closed while the compressor delivers vapour to the tanker side
Hot weather – vapour pressure 16 barg at 50 °C
Liquid overfill – no vapour space left (see N01-06)
Vapour drawn off faster than the liquid vaporises in winter
Transfer not stopped at high level (source)
Wrong ullage – delivery larger than the free volume
Level transmitter LT-11/21/31 reads low (drift, stuck float)
Pool fire from a release at the unloading bay
Rapid depressurisation / venting of liquid propane (auto-refrigeration to −42 °C)
Liquid leak through a valve – flashing liquid chills the line
Unloading arm or hose failure (wear, kinking, wrong gasket)
Driver moves the tanker before disconnection
Isolation by a single valve; liquid trapped between valves
Purge not complete before hot work
Low liquid level in the bullet
High liquid temperature (summer) – low NPSH margin
Vaporiser over-heating raises the pressure upstream
Liquid blocked in between closed valves and heated (thermal expansion)
Corrosion under insulation at the liquid lines
Loss of propane vapour supply (vaporiser trip, PCV-01 closes, header low pressure)
FFIC-01 propane flow transmitter fails high
FFIC-01 fails / air flow transmitter fails low
Blower trip with propane pressure higher than the air side
Users' fuel valves close quickly (load rejection)
Purge not done or incomplete after maintenance
Blowers started before propane is established
Header pressure lower than furnace pressure
Burner flashback when the mixture is near the flammable range

safeguards.description: Standby vapour compressor available (source)
Compressor discharge high-pressure trip at 20.6 barg (source: 21 kg/cm2)
Tanker designed for 20.6 barg; bullets designed for 17.5 barg (source)
Pressure gauges PG-01, PG-12, PG-13, PG-14 on the unloading header and bullets; tanker pressure gauge (source)
Bullet relief valves PSV-11/21/31 at 17.5 barg, fire-case sized, discharging vertically upwards (source: 'PSV provided')
Thermal relief valve PRV-01 on the unloading liquid line (source)
Tanker, line and tanks earthed; earth bonding interlock EBI-1 prevents compressor start without a verified tanker earth
Gas leak detectors GLD-1, GLD-2, GLD-3 at the unloading bay and tank farm with alarm (source)
Water sprinklers on the bullets and the tanker unloading station (source), 10 l/min/m2
High-high level trip LAHH (85 %) from LT-11/21/31 closes ROV-11/21/31 and stops the compressors (source: LT closes ROV)
High level alarm LAH at 80 % with operator response (stop unloading)
Tanker unloading procedure OP-PR-010 and checklist: ullage check before unloading, operator in attendance throughout
All ROVs and solenoid valves fail closed on loss of power or air (source)
Emergency release coupling ERC-1 on the unloading arm with self-closing valves on both sides
Tanker brake interlock and wheel chocks; keys held by the unloading operator
Gas detection GLD-1/2/3 (1oo3) and manual ESD ESD-1 close ROV-1 and ROV-11/21/31 and stop C-01/C-02/C-03 (logic UCP-1)
Manual ESD push buttons at the unloading bay, tank farm and control room
Unloading arm / hose inspection and annual pressure test; leak test before each transfer
Bullets and liquid lines in low-temperature carbon steel (design min. −45 °C)
Depressurisation procedure: no rapid venting of liquid-full equipment; vent only vapour to the flare stack
Ignition source control – Ex equipment in zoned areas, hot-work permits, vehicle control, no mobile phones at the bay
Separation distances to buildings, roads and the furnace area; bunded / kerbed impoundment sloped away from the bullets
Emergency response team and fire brigade; LPG emergency plan (cooling, evacuation radius)
Pump minimum-flow recycle and low-suction-pressure trip
Double mechanical seals with seal-pot pressure alarm on P-01/P-02
Vaporiser bath temperature control with duty / standby vaporisers
Low vapour outlet temperature trip TSL-01 (10 °C) closes the vaporiser liquid inlet
High liquid level trip LSH-01 in the vaporiser shell closes the liquid inlet (liquid carry-over protection)
Vaporiser relief valve PSV-02 at 20 barg
Slam-shut valve SSV-01 upstream of PCV-01 closes at 2.5 barg (over-pressure shut-off)
Vapour header relief valve PSV-03 at 3.0 barg to a safe location
Vapour header pressure alarms PAH / PAL on PT-02 with operator response
Low-low fuel pressure trips in the users' burner management systems
Propane / air ratio controller FFIC-01 with cross-limiting (air follows propane)
Low propane pressure trip PSLL-01: stops B-01/B-02 and closes XV-01 / XV-02 (mixture trip)
Calorimeter / Wobbe analyser AT-01 with low-heating-value trip (independent of FFIC-01)
In-line flame arrester FA-01 on the propane–air header to the users
Explosion vent panel EP-01 on surge tank ST-01
Surge tank relief valve PSV-04 at 2.0 barg
Start-up procedure OP-PR-020: N2 purge of mixer and surge tank, propane established before air, mixture verified by AT-01 before supply
Non-return valve NRV-01 on the air line to MX-01 (prevents propane back-flow into the blowers)
UPS for UCP-1 and the gas detection (30 min); ROVs fail closed
Permit-to-work with isolation verification, N2 purge / gas-free test and fire watch
Proof testing – annual trip tests of the overfill and mixture trips; quarterly gas-detector bump tests

recs.text: Provide copper / aluminium / G.I. jumper strips for electrical continuity at every flange of the unloading line, check the resistance of all earthing strips and pits and keep a record; add an earth bonding interlock (EBI-1) so the compressors cannot start without a verified tanker earth (source recommendation no. 1, completed).

Provide a diesel generator for back-up power to the propane storage system so that a power failure during unloading or supply leaves the system in a controlled state (source recommendation no. 2). Confirm that every ROV fails closed and that UCP-1 and the gas detection are on UPS-1.
Add the bullet relief valves PSV-11/21/31 and PRV-01 to the statutory inspection schedule with a 2-yearly bench-test interval (source remark, made a recommendation).

Make the overfill trip independent of the level gauge used for control: fit an independent high-high level switch on each bullet acting on ROV-11/21/31, and proof-test the trip every 6 months. Fault tree FT-PR-01 gives an overfill frequency of 1.9E-3 /yr with the protection PFDavg 3.9E-3.
Add a written ullage calculation to the unloading checklist (volume in the bullet + delivery ≤ 85 %), signed before the compressor is started.
Fit an emergency release coupling ERC-1 and a tanker brake interlock at the unloading bay; drive-away during unloading is not covered by the source safeguards.

Confirm that the bullets, the liquid lines and the unloading arm are rated for −45 °C (auto-refrigeration of propane on rapid depressurisation); the source worksheet recorded 'Lower temperature – no issue'.

Verify the gas detection and ESD function against the required risk reduction: fault tree FT-PR-03 gives PFDavg 3.9E-2; relocate GLD-1/2/3 at low level (propane vapour is heavier than air) and add a detector at the compressor house.
Check the bullet sprinkler / deluge coverage and density against the fire-case relief study and add automatic start on fire detection at the unloading bay (BLEVE prevention); test annually.
Fit a low-suction-pressure trip and seal-pot alarm on P-01/P-02; replace single seals with double mechanical seals.
Provide a second, independent liquid carry-over protection on each vaporiser (high-level trip LSH-01 in addition to TSL-01) and test both every 6 months.
Confirm the set-point staggering of PCV-01 (1.5 barg), SSV-01 (2.5 barg) and PSV-03 (3.0 barg) against the vapour header design pressure (3.5 barg).

Upgrade the propane–air mixture protection: make the calorimeter AT-01 trip independent of FFIC-01 and add a second low propane pressure switch (1oo2). Fault tree FT-PR-02 gives a flammable-mixture frequency of 1.2E-2 /yr (protection PFDavg 1.8E-2); bow tie BT-PR-02 internal explosion 7.6E-5 /yr.
Rewrite the mixing-station start-up procedure OP-PR-020: N2 purge, propane established before air, AT-01 reading verified before the users are opened; add a start-permissive interlock.
Inspect flame arrester FA-01 every 6 months (fouling) and confirm it is rated for the propane–air mixture and pipe length (in-line deflagration arrester).
Introduce a vehicle-movement plan for the unloading bay (no other traffic during unloading, crash barriers around the bullets and the arm).

Train LPG operators on the response to a release (ESD, evacuation upwind, no attempt to stop a burning leak, cooling of exposed vessels) with a drill twice a year; event tree ETA-PR-01 gives 1.2E-5 /yr for a vapour cloud explosion or BLEVE.
